tasks.task: Establish site, scaffold, and occupant interface plan
tasks.scope: Site induction, scaffold erection to all four elevations, exclusion zones below working edge, occupied-building interfaces on ground and first floors, emergency procedures, site signage and barriers.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker slip or trip during scaffold erection on uneven or wet ground
Struck by scaffold components — dropped or misaligned members during erection
Collapse or instability of incomplete scaffold — load applied before bracing complete
Struck by vehicle — site traffic in proximity to scaffold footprint during erection
Electrical contact — scaffold erected near or touching overhead powerlines
tasks.dominant_hazard: Collapse or instability of incomplete scaffold during erection
controls: Confirm scaffold design and load calculations signed by engineer before erection starts.
Mark and exclude all areas below working edge with 100% compliant barriers — minimum 1.2 m height or full netting.
Barricade vehicle access within 5 m of scaffold footprint — traffic controller present during erection.
Check overhead powerlines clearance minimum 3 m horizontal distance — de-energise or isolate if closer.
check ground bearing surface — compact soil, level concrete, or approved bearing plates. Stop work if soft, sloping, or contaminated.
Erect bracing and cross-bracing in strict design sequence — no work at height until lower sections fully braced.
Secure all scaffold connections using approved couplers — no bolt substitution or temporary lashing.
Install guardrails and mid-rails to all working edges — 1.1 m top rail, 0.5 m mid-rail, maximum 0.5 m gap to edge.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold above base height until: ground bearing condition checked and approved by supervising scaffolder.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker access to completed scaffold until: handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder and all bracing visible complete.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ground bearing subsides, shifts, or differs from design — re-check and re-approve before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: overhead powerline clearance cannot be maintained — contact network operator and de-energise or isolate before proceeding.
🛑 STOP WORK if: vehicle or pedestrian breaches exclusion zone during erection — re-establish barriers and traffic control before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Remove existing render, failed sealants, and loose concrete spall
tasks.scope: Mechanical removal of failed acrylic render, concrete spalling, and failed sealant from all elevations. Silica-producing demolition work. Dust and noise controls. Debris containment and removal from occupied-building exclusion zone
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loss of balance or slip on wet or dusty scaffold platform
Struck by falling debris — loose render or spall fragments ejected downward toward occupied-building exclusion zone or personnel below
Noise-induced hearing damage — mechanical removal tool use without adequate hearing protection (noise >85 dB)
Eye injury — fine concrete or render particles striking unprotected eyes during high-energy removal
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust — respirable silica from mechanical render and concrete removal
controls: Suppress dust at source using wet cutting or grinder attachment with integrated water feed — no dry grinding, angle grinder fitted with wet suppression shroud only.
Provide local dust extraction — handheld grinder connected to HEPA-filter dust extractor with minimum 150 L/min airflow, positioned to capture dust at tool point.
Erect dust containment barrier around work area — clear plastic sheeting sealed to scaffold to contain debris and prevent fallout into occupied zone below.
Verify SDS for render composition on site before work starts — confirm asbestos status and silica content with site supervisor.
Rotate workers on high-exposure tasks (grinding, cutting, spalling removal) — no single worker exceeds 2 hours continuous mechanical removal per shift.
Barricade exclusion zone below work area — sign and erect physical barrier to prevent unauthorised entry; verify zone is clear before each tool start.
Check scaffold platform before each shift — confirm handrails intact, platform clear of debris and pooled water, no trip hazards or loose planking.
Maintain three-point contact during access and egress — no running, jumping, or working on wet or dusty surfaces; use taglines for tool transfer.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start mechanical removal until: Site supervisor confirms SDS review complete, asbestos status confirmed clear, and dust extraction system tested and operational.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow first worker onto completed scaffold until: Licenced scaffolder provides signed handover certificate and all harness anchor points are tagged and load-tested.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Dust suppression system fails, water feed stops, or grinder operates dry for >1 minute.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Debris escapes containment barrier, falls outside exclusion zone, or strikes building below.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Worker slips, loses balance, or loses three-point contact on scaffold platform; check cause before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.scope: Remove remaining loose material, dust vacuum, expose full extent of cracks, spalling, carbonation, and render delamination. Document damage with photographs. Identify areas requiring structural stitching versus patch repair.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of dust — vacuum extraction failure or inadequate dust suppression during loose material removal
Fall from height — worker overreaching or loss of balance during close-proximity assessment of cracks and spalling
Struck by falling tools or instruments — dropped measuring device, camera, or pencil from scaffold platform
Asbestos disturbance — latent risk if sealants, adhesives, or coatings contain asbestos (unconfirmed but common in older render systems)
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of dust — inadequate suppression or vacuum extraction failure
controls: Operate HEPA dust extractor continuously during loose material removal — position extraction hose within 300mm of work zone.
Wet-suppress all loose material before removal — spray with water mist or damp cloth to suppress airborne dust.
Check HEPA filter condition and airflow before each shift — replace if bypass or loss of suction occurs.
Prohibit dry grinding, chipping, or abrasive removal — all dust-generating work must use wet suppression or extraction.
Secure all hand tools and instruments (measuring tape, pencil, camera) to scaffold rail via lanyard — no unsecured items on platform.
Position worker harness attachment at scaffold frame — maintain connection whenever reaching beyond arm's length to assess cracks or spalling.
Barricade working perimeter 2m below scaffold — restrict access to exclusion zone; post 'Falling Objects' signage on scaffold.
Document all asbestos-suspect materials (sealants, adhesives, coatings) with photographs before disturbance — flag for lab analysis if uncertain of age or composition.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not expose substrate using power tools until: HEPA dust extractor tested, airflow verified, and wet suppression system operational.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not document or photograph asbestos-suspect sealants or coatings until: material sample collected and flagged for lab analysis confirmation.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: HEPA vacuum suction loss or filter bypass detected — do not resume until filter replaced and airflow restored.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses harness connection or steps beyond barricade — do not resume until connection reattached and perimeter re-secured.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unknown friable material, discoloured render, or suspected asbestos coating is exposed — do not proceed until lab confirmation received.

tasks.task: Execute crack stitching and concrete repair
tasks.scope: Install helical stitches across cracks per design. Patch spalled areas with concrete repair mortar, level to substrate plane. Cure per product specification. Target remedial repair to structural integrity and appearance.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loss of balance or overreach while installing helical stitches at high elevation
Struck by hand tools or materials — dropped stitching anchor, wrench, or repair mortar container during application
Chemical exposure — inhalation of fumes or skin contact with uncured concrete repair mortar or adhesive
Inadequate curing — premature loading or exposure to rain before cure-time compliance, resulting in repair failure
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — loss of balance or overreach during stitch installation at elevation
controls: Wear full body harness tethered to certified anchor point before starting stitch installation at height.
Install edge protection or guardrail around work perimeter — minimum 1.1 m high — before starting work.
Establish exclusion zone directly below work area — barricade and delineate with caution tape — keep public and workers out.
Secure all hand tools and materials in tool belt or lanyard — no loose items on scaffold or at height.
Review SDS for concrete repair mortar and epoxy resin anchors on point of use — confirm ventilation and skin contact PPE match product requirements.
Ventilate work area continuously — open-side work or mechanical fan — during application and initial cure window.
Apply repair mortar only to dry, clean substrate — remove loose concrete, dust, and contaminants with wire brush and vacuum before application.
Apply mortar in weather window only — no rain forecast for 24 hours post-application — confirm with site supervisor before starting.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install helical stitches or apply repair mortar until: scaffold erected, inspected, and handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply repair mortar until: substrate dry, cleaned, approved by supervisor, and weather window (no rain for 24 hours) confirmed.

tasks.scope: Walk-over inspection of all elevations. Check coating coverage, colour uniformity, texture consistency, crack stitching visible, no defects. Identify any touch-up or remedial work required.

Weather exposure — prolonged inspection in high wind, rain, or cold conditions causing loss of grip or concentration
Incomplete or defective repair — undetected coating defects, colour mismatches, or stitching inadequacy requiring rework
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — loss of balance or slip during platform walk-over inspection
controls: Confirm coating substrate is dry and grip tested before inspection platform walk-over commences.
Establish 1.5 m exclusion zone below inspection platform. Post signage and barricade zone with safety netting or catch net.
Conduct platform surface condition check before each shift — test foot grip, identify algae, moss, or wet patches, remove slippery debris.
Wear non-slip footwear with verified grip rating (AS/NZS 2210.3) — test grip on wet platform before starting.
Secure inspection torch, magnifying glass, and sample colour swatches in tool belt — never carry loose in hands.
Establish weather stop rule: suspend inspection if wind speed exceeds 40 km/h, rain reduces visibility below 10 m, or platform becomes visibly wet.
Brief all workers on defect identification criteria before inspection — photograph reference samples of acceptable colour match, texture consistency, crack stitch visibility.
check in pairs — one worker on platform, one spotter on adjacent scaffold bay. Spotter maintains visual contact and confirms platform stability.

tasks.task: Confirm scaffold safety, load capacity, and edge protection
tasks.scope: Pre-work inspection of scaffold platform safety, guardrails, toe boards, handholds, load-rating for personnel and materials, wind assessment, certification review before work commences.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — guardrail or toeboard failure not detected before use
Overload failure — platform load capacity breached by personnel, materials, or equipment
Inadequate handholds — worker loss of grip or balance on slippery or absent handholds
Wind-induced collapse — scaffold not adequately braced or stability compromised by wind gusts >20 knots
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — guardrail failure not detected before use
controls: Obtain and review scaffold erection permit and handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses platform.
Check all guardrails for damage, loose fixings, or gaps; measure height from platform to top rail — must be 950–1150 mm.
Check toeboard height minimum 100 mm and check for splits, loose fixings, or missing sections along full platform length.
Verify handholds are continuous, secure, and free from grease or contamination; confirm grip diameter 25–40 mm for comfortable grip.
Confirm platform load capacity label is visible and legible; work out total load (personnel + materials + equipment) and verify does not exceed rated capacity.
Conduct wind assessment — stop work if sustained wind exceeds 20 knots or gusts exceed 25 knots; confirm bracing and guy-ropes are taut and undamaged.
Confirm scaffold is tagged 'SAFE TO USE' by licenced scaffolder within last 7 days; check tag date and scaffolder name against permit.
Brief all workers on platform load limit, exclusion zones below scaffold, and fall arrest requirements before work commences.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker onto scaffold platform until: licenced scaffolder has signed handover certificate and 'SAFE TO USE' tag is current and visible.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not position materials or equipment on platform until: load calculation is confirmed and total load is verified below rated capacity.

🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 20 knots sustained or gusts exceed 25 knots.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold 'SAFE TO USE' tag is absent, outdated, or platform load is approached or exceeded.

tasks.task: Prime and prepare repaired substrate
tasks.scope: Apply primer coat to all repaired concrete and exposed substrate. Allow cure. Light sand or damp-wipe to remove dust. Ready substrate for anti-carbonation coating application.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of primer vapours — inadequate ventilation or respiratory protection during primer application
Fall from height — slippery scaffold platform from wet primer drips or splashes
Chemical skin contact — uncured primer contact causing irritation or sensitisation
Fire or explosion hazard — primer vapour accumulation in low-wind conditions or near ignition source
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of primer vapours — inadequate ventilation during application
controls: Verify SDS on point of use before primer application starts. Check Section 8 (exposure controls) for organic vapour respirator requirement and ventilation threshold.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation or natural airflow (minimum 0.5 m/s cross-breeze) across work area during primer application and for full cure window stated on SDS.
Wear organic vapour respirator (APF 10, per SDS Section 8) if ventilation cannot be confirmed or wind drops below minimum threshold during application.
Restrict access to scaffold platform during primer application. Post 'Wet Primer — Do Not Enter' sign at access point until surface is touch-dry (time per SDS).
Wipe or sweep wet primer drips from scaffold platform edge and walkways immediately after application using lint-free cloth or damp cloth — no dry sweeping.
Allow full cure time stated on SDS before light sanding or damp-wiping substrate. Record cure start time and sign-off time on job sheet.
Use damp cloth or vacuum-equipped sander (HEPA filter, silica dust suppression) for residual dust removal. Never dry-sand cured primer coat.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile minimum; check SDS for upgrade to butyl or neoprene if specified) during primer application and cleanup.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer until: SDS has been reviewed on point of use, ventilation requirement confirmed, and organic vapour respirator fitted and tested if required by SDS Section 8.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply anti-carbonation coating until: substrate cure time confirmed complete (per SDS Section 5), light sanding or damp-wiping finished, and substrate is visually clean and dry.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind drops below minimum ventilation threshold stated on SDS, or worker reports dizziness, nausea, or headache during primer application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: primer vapour is visible as mist or haze across work area, or air quality cannot be confirmed as safe during application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold platform becomes slippery from primer splash, or wet primer drips cannot be managed without creating fall hazard.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Wear organic vapour respirator (cartridge type per SDS Section 8) fitted and checked before each coat application. Do not use P2 dust masks for solvent or resin vapours.

check scaffold platform before each shift for wet drips, overspray, or slippery surface. Clean or dry affected areas with absorbent cloth before resuming work. Prohibit barefoot or smooth-soled footwear on platform.
Apply first coat in thin, even passes. Do not re-wet or overload substrate. Allow full cure time per SDS before second coat — minimum 16 hours or as specified by manufacturer, verified in writing.
Establish wet coating exclusion zone on scaffold platform — barricade wet areas with warning tape and cones. Post 'Wet Paint' signage visible to all workers and building occupants.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or butyl per SDS) and hi-viz shirt or vest
Do not start second coat until substrate is fully cured and inspected for even coverage. Check for bare patches, thin areas, or colour mismatch — mark and fix before final coat.

task_blocks_raw.scope: Site induction, scaffold erection to all four elevations, exclusion zones below working edge, occupied-building interfaces on ground and first floors, emergency procedures, site signage and barriers.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker slip or trip during scaffold erection on uneven or wet ground
Struck by scaffold components — dropped or misaligned members during erection
Collapse or instability of incomplete scaffold — load applied before bracing complete
Struck by vehicle — site traffic in proximity to scaffold footprint during erection
Electrical contact — scaffold erected near or touching overhead powerlines
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Collapse or instability of incomplete scaffold during erection
controls: Confirm scaffold design and load calculations signed by engineer before erection starts.
Mark and exclude all areas below working edge with 100% compliant barriers — minimum 1.2 m height or full netting.
Barricade vehicle access within 5 m of scaffold footprint — traffic controller present during erection.
Check overhead powerlines clearance minimum 3 m horizontal distance — de-energise or isolate if closer.
check ground bearing surface — compact soil, level concrete, or approved bearing plates. Stop work if soft, sloping, or contaminated.
Erect bracing and cross-bracing in strict design sequence — no work at height until lower sections fully braced.
Secure all scaffold connections using approved couplers — no bolt substitution or temporary lashing.
Install guardrails and mid-rails to all working edges — 1.1 m top rail, 0.5 m mid-rail, maximum 0.5 m gap to edge.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold above base height until: ground bearing condition checked and approved by supervising scaffolder.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker access to completed scaffold until: handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder and all bracing visible complete.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ground bearing subsides, shifts, or differs from design — re-check and re-approve before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: overhead powerline clearance cannot be maintained — contact network operator and de-energise or isolate before proceeding.
🛑 STOP WORK if: vehicle or pedestrian breaches exclusion zone during erection — re-establish barriers and traffic control before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Handover certificate — signed by licenced scaffolder before first worker access.
Working at heights permit — signed by supervisor before any elevated work.
Noise management plan — delivered to building management and occupants before site start.
Site induction register — completed and signed by all workers before site entry.
Ground bearing assessment — documented by supervising scaffolder before erection.
Occupant notification letter — delivered minimum 5 working days before erection; emergency contact number provided.

Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: steel-capped footwear— ankle support, steel toe, slip-resistant
Harness and lanyard — inspected and compliant to AS/NZS 1891.1 — for workers at height during erection

monitoring.critical_control: Confirm bracing installation matches scaffold design before load applied — visual check by supervising scaffolder each shift.
monitoring.frequency: Before erection commences, after each major section completion, daily during erection, before handover
monitoring.evidence: Erection plan signed off with dated photographs showing bracing at each level; handover certificate counter-signed

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

task_blocks_raw.task: Confirm scaffold safety, load capacity, and edge protection
task_blocks_raw.scope: Pre-work inspection of scaffold platform safety, guardrails, toe boards, handholds, load-rating for personnel and materials, wind assessment, certification review before work commences.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — guardrail or toeboard failure not detected before use
Overload failure — platform load capacity breached by personnel, materials, or equipment
Inadequate handholds — worker loss of grip or balance on slippery or absent handholds
Wind-induced collapse — scaffold not adequately braced or stability compromised by wind gusts >20 knots
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — guardrail failure not detected before use
controls: Obtain and review scaffold erection permit and handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses platform.
Check all guardrails for damage, loose fixings, or gaps; measure height from platform to top rail — must be 950–1150 mm.
Check toeboard height minimum 100 mm and check for splits, loose fixings, or missing sections along full platform length.
Verify handholds are continuous, secure, and free from grease or contamination; confirm grip diameter 25–40 mm for comfortable grip.
Confirm platform load capacity label is visible and legible; work out total load (personnel + materials + equipment) and verify does not exceed rated capacity.
Conduct wind assessment — stop work if sustained wind exceeds 20 knots or gusts exceed 25 knots; confirm bracing and guy-ropes are taut and undamaged.
Confirm scaffold is tagged 'SAFE TO USE' by licenced scaffolder within last 7 days; check tag date and scaffolder name against permit.
Brief all workers on platform load limit, exclusion zones below scaffold, and fall arrest requirements before work commences.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker onto scaffold platform until: licenced scaffolder has signed handover certificate and 'SAFE TO USE' tag is current and visible.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not position materials or equipment on platform until: load calculation is confirmed and total load is verified below rated capacity.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: guardrail height is below 950 mm, toeboard is missing or damaged, or handholds are not continuous.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 20 knots sustained or gusts exceed 25 knots.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold 'SAFE TO USE' tag is absent, outdated, or platform load is approached or exceeded.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Maintain register of scaffold inspection sign-offs — record date, time, inspector name, and any defects identified.
tell site supervisor and licenced scaffolder immediately if any defect is found; do not permit workaround repairs — only licenced scaffolder may remediate.
Repeat pre-work scaffold check daily and after any weather event, high wind, or vibration-generating work on adjacent floors.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

monitoring.critical_control: Check guardrail height, toeboard integrity, handhold continuity, and 'SAFE TO USE' tag daily before any worker access.
monitoring.frequency: daily before work starts, after weather events, after high-impact work on adjacent levels
monitoring.evidence: Daily scaffold inspection checklist completed and filed; 'SAFE TO USE' tag visible and current; no defects recorded.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove existing render, failed sealants, and loose concrete spall
task_blocks_raw.scope: Mechanical removal of failed acrylic render, concrete spalling, and failed sealant from all elevations. Silica-producing demolition work. Dust and noise controls. Debris containment and removal from occupied-building exclusion zone
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loss of balance or slip on wet or dusty scaffold platform
Struck by falling debris — loose render or spall fragments ejected downward toward occupied-building exclusion zone or personnel below
Noise-induced hearing damage — mechanical removal tool use without adequate hearing protection (noise >85 dB)
Eye injury — fine concrete or render particles striking unprotected eyes during high-energy removal
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust — respirable silica from mechanical render and concrete removal
controls: Suppress dust at source using wet cutting or grinder attachment with integrated water feed — no dry grinding, angle grinder fitted with wet suppression shroud only.
Provide local dust extraction — handheld grinder connected to HEPA-filter dust extractor with minimum 150 L/min airflow, positioned to capture dust at tool point.
Erect dust containment barrier around work area — clear plastic sheeting sealed to scaffold to contain debris and prevent fallout into occupied zone below.
Verify SDS for render composition on site before work starts — confirm asbestos status and silica content with site supervisor.
Rotate workers on high-exposure tasks (grinding, cutting, spalling removal) — no single worker exceeds 2 hours continuous mechanical removal per shift.
Barricade exclusion zone below work area — sign and erect physical barrier to prevent unauthorised entry; verify zone is clear before each tool start.
Check scaffold platform before each shift — confirm handrails intact, platform clear of debris and pooled water, no trip hazards or loose planking.
Maintain three-point contact during access and egress — no running, jumping, or working on wet or dusty surfaces; use taglines for tool transfer.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start mechanical removal until: Site supervisor confirms SDS review complete, asbestos status confirmed clear, and dust extraction system tested and operational.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow first worker onto completed scaffold until: Licenced scaffolder provides signed handover certificate and all harness anchor points are tagged and load-tested.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Dust suppression system fails, water feed stops, or grinder operates dry for >1 minute.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Debris escapes containment barrier, falls outside exclusion zone, or strikes building below.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Worker slips, loses balance, or loses three-point contact on scaffold platform; check cause before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Obtain signed working-at-heights permit before each elevated task; display on site.
Obtain noise management plan from project manager and distribute to all workers; include measures for nearby occupants.
Verify White Card (CPCCWHS1001) induction current for all workers before site entry.
Verify scaffolding licence (class appropriate to type and height) held by erecting scaffolder; record on site.
Verify working-at-heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent) held by all workers using scaffold; record current currency.

Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Organic vapour respirator or P3 particulate mask rated for respirable silica and concrete dust — fit-tested and worn continuous during mechanical removal.
Hard hat with integrated ear cups or helmet with separately mounted earmuffs rated to achieve minimum 27 dB(A) noise reduction.
High-visibility vest (Class D) visible from all directions.

monitoring.critical_control: Verify water feed to grinder active before each removal cycle; confirm dust extraction audible and air speed ≥150 L/min.
monitoring.frequency: Before each tool start and every 30 minutes continuous work
monitoring.evidence: Visual check of water spray and dust collector fill; sound log if noise >85 dB(A)

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

task_blocks_raw.task: Expose concrete substrate and assess damage
task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove remaining loose material, dust vacuum, expose full extent of cracks, spalling, carbonation, and render delamination. Document damage with photographs. Identify areas requiring structural stitching versus patch repair.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of dust — vacuum extraction failure or inadequate dust suppression during loose material removal
Fall from height — worker overreaching or loss of balance during close-proximity assessment of cracks and spalling
Struck by falling tools or instruments — dropped measuring device, camera, or pencil from scaffold platform
Asbestos disturbance — latent risk if sealants, adhesives, or coatings contain asbestos (unconfirmed but common in older render systems)
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of dust — inadequate suppression or vacuum extraction failure
controls: Operate HEPA dust extractor continuously during loose material removal — position extraction hose within 300mm of work zone.
Wet-suppress all loose material before removal — spray with water mist or damp cloth to suppress airborne dust.
Check HEPA filter condition and airflow before each shift — replace if bypass or loss of suction occurs.
Prohibit dry grinding, chipping, or abrasive removal — all dust-generating work must use wet suppression or extraction.
Secure all hand tools and instruments (measuring tape, pencil, camera) to scaffold rail via lanyard — no unsecured items on platform.
Position worker harness attachment at scaffold frame — maintain connection whenever reaching beyond arm's length to assess cracks or spalling.
Barricade working perimeter 2m below scaffold — restrict access to exclusion zone; post 'Falling Objects' signage on scaffold.
Document all asbestos-suspect materials (sealants, adhesives, coatings) with photographs before disturbance — flag for lab analysis if uncertain of age or composition.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not expose substrate using power tools until: HEPA dust extractor tested, airflow verified, and wet suppression system operational.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not document or photograph asbestos-suspect sealants or coatings until: material sample collected and flagged for lab analysis confirmation.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: HEPA vacuum suction loss or filter bypass detected — do not resume until filter replaced and airflow restored.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses harness connection or steps beyond barricade — do not resume until connection reattached and perimeter re-secured.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unknown friable material, discoloured render, or suspected asbestos coating is exposed — do not proceed until lab confirmation received.
admin: Verify scaffold erection permit and handover certificate before any worker accesses platform.
Confirm working at heights permit signed and current competency verified (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Obtain SDS for any chemical sealants, adhesives, or repair primers before exposure assessment commences.
tell building occupants of dust suppression work — provide warning if extraction noise or vibration affects occupied spaces.
Record vacuum filter change, extraction airflow test, and asbestos-suspect material flags in site diary with date and initials.
ppe: P2 particulate respirator (fit-tested) — continuous use during loose material removal and dust-generating tasks.
eye protection— protect eyes from dust and spalling debris during close inspection.
High-visibility vest or harness with integrated identifier — required for all scaffold work.
Hard hat — mandatory on scaffold platform.
Steel-capped boots — required on scaffold and ground level.

monitoring.critical_control: HEPA vacuum airflow test — compare pre-shift and mid-shift suction pressure; filter visual check for dust bypass or visible damage.
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift start; every 2 hours during active dust generation; immediately after filter change.
monitoring.evidence: Vacuum airflow gauge reading recorded in site diary; filter change tag dated; worker sign-off sheet confirming extraction operational confirmation.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

task_blocks_raw.task: Execute crack stitching and concrete repair
task_blocks_raw.scope: Install helical stitches across cracks per design. Patch spalled areas with concrete repair mortar, level to substrate plane. Cure per product specification. Target remedial repair to structural integrity and appearance.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loss of balance or overreach while installing helical stitches at high elevation
Struck by hand tools or materials — dropped stitching anchor, wrench, or repair mortar container during application
Chemical exposure — inhalation of fumes or skin contact with uncured concrete repair mortar or adhesive
Inadequate curing — premature loading or exposure to rain before cure-time compliance, resulting in repair failure
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — loss of balance or overreach during stitch installation at elevation
controls: Wear full body harness tethered to certified anchor point before starting stitch installation at height.
Install edge protection or guardrail around work perimeter — minimum 1.1 m high — before starting work.
Establish exclusion zone directly below work area — barricade and delineate with caution tape — keep public and workers out.
Secure all hand tools and materials in tool belt or lanyard — no loose items on scaffold or at height.
Review SDS for concrete repair mortar and epoxy resin anchors on point of use — confirm ventilation and skin contact PPE match product requirements.
Ventilate work area continuously — open-side work or mechanical fan — during application and initial cure window.
Apply repair mortar only to dry, clean substrate — remove loose concrete, dust, and contaminants with wire brush and vacuum before application.
Apply mortar in weather window only — no rain forecast for 24 hours post-application — confirm with site supervisor before starting.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install helical stitches or apply repair mortar until: scaffold erected, inspected, and handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply repair mortar until: substrate dry, cleaned, approved by supervisor, and weather window (no rain for 24 hours) confirmed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: harness anchor point fails, edge protection is damaged or incomplete, or worker loses balance or shows signs of overreach.
🛑 STOP WORK if: rain begins or forecast changes to rain within 24-hour cure window — halt application and cover wet areas with plastic sheeting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: SDS requirements for ventilation or PPE cannot be met, or chemical exposure symptoms (dizziness, skin irritation) occur.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display scaffold erection permit and handover certificate before any work at height starts.
Obtain and display working at heights permit signed by supervisor before each elevated task.
Brief all workers on fall arrest and rescue procedure at start of shift.
Record completion date and cure-time start on repair schedule — attach photographic evidence of completed area.
Conduct final inspection after cure time elapsed — check repair adhesion, surface finish, and cure hardness before sign-off.
tell building occupants of noise and odour during application — provide warning notice at site entry.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Full body harness (Class 1, minimum load rating 130 kg, harness checked for damage before each use)
Organic vapour respirator (per SDS Section 8 — not P2 dust mask) when applying epoxy or polyurethane anchors or mortar in low-ventilation areas

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift start and continuous during elevated work
monitoring.evidence: Visual harness and anchor inspection checklist — dated and signed by supervisor; photographic record of anchor point installation.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply primer coat to all repaired concrete and exposed substrate. Allow cure. Light sand or damp-wipe to remove dust. Ready substrate for anti-carbonation coating application.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of primer vapours — inadequate ventilation or respiratory protection during primer application
Fall from height — slippery scaffold platform from wet primer drips or splashes
Chemical skin contact — uncured primer contact causing irritation or sensitisation
Fire or explosion hazard — primer vapour accumulation in low-wind conditions or near ignition source
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of primer vapours — inadequate ventilation during application
controls: Verify SDS on point of use before primer application starts. Check Section 8 (exposure controls) for organic vapour respirator requirement and ventilation threshold.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation or natural airflow (minimum 0.5 m/s cross-breeze) across work area during primer application and for full cure window stated on SDS.
Wear organic vapour respirator (APF 10, per SDS Section 8) if ventilation cannot be confirmed or wind drops below minimum threshold during application.
Restrict access to scaffold platform during primer application. Post 'Wet Primer — Do Not Enter' sign at access point until surface is touch-dry (time per SDS).
Wipe or sweep wet primer drips from scaffold platform edge and walkways immediately after application using lint-free cloth or damp cloth — no dry sweeping.
Allow full cure time stated on SDS before light sanding or damp-wiping substrate. Record cure start time and sign-off time on job sheet.
Use damp cloth or vacuum-equipped sander (HEPA filter, silica dust suppression) for residual dust removal. Never dry-sand cured primer coat.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile minimum; check SDS for upgrade to butyl or neoprene if specified) during primer application and cleanup.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer until: SDS has been reviewed on point of use, ventilation requirement confirmed, and organic vapour respirator fitted and tested if required by SDS Section 8.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply anti-carbonation coating until: substrate cure time confirmed complete (per SDS Section 5), light sanding or damp-wiping finished, and substrate is visually clean and dry.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind drops below minimum ventilation threshold stated on SDS, or worker reports dizziness, nausea, or headache during primer application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: primer vapour is visible as mist or haze across work area, or air quality cannot be confirmed as safe during application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold platform becomes slippery from primer splash, or wet primer drips cannot be managed without creating fall hazard.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: tell site induction co-ordinator and site supervisor of primer application schedule 24 hours before work. Include ventilation plan, exclusion zone, fire watch requirement.
Record on daily work log: primer application start time, ventilation method (mechanical / natural), organic vapour respirator use (yes/no), cure window start time, cure completion time.
Obtain current SDS from primer supplier before application. Confirm Section 8 organic vapour threshold, cure time (Section 5), and skin contact first aid (Section 4).
Conduct safety talk with all workers on access restriction, slippery platform hazard, and chemical contact protocol immediately before primer application.
Establish fire watch: stationary spotter positioned upwind of primer application area during application and for period specified on SDS (typically 30–60 min post-application).
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (APF 10) — fitted, tested, and worn continuous during primer application if ventilation threshold cannot be met
Hard hat (scaffold bumps; mandatory on all elevated work)

monitoring.critical_control: Confirm continuous mechanical ventilation or minimum 0.5 m/s cross-breeze across work area. Record wind speed or fan setting before primer application and at 30 min intervals.
monitoring.frequency: Before application start, continuous during application, and at 30 min intervals during cure window
monitoring.evidence: Anemometer reading (natural ventilation) or fan status log (mechanical ventilation). Operator sign-off on job sheet confirming ventilation threshold met. SDS Section 8 requirement documented.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Prime and prepare repaired substrate
responsibility.WKR: Perform Prime and prepare repaired substrate per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply anti-carbonation coating to all facade elevations per manufacturer specification. Two coats minimum or as specified. Cure fully between coats. Allow specified cure time before finish coat application.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of coating vapours — inadequate ventilation or respiratory protection during application of multi-coat system
Fall from height — slippery scaffold platform from wet coating drips or overspray
Chemical exposure — skin contact with uncured coating causing irritation or allergic reaction
Poor coating coverage — inadequate application or curing conditions resulting in uneven protection and corrosion risk
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of coating vapours — inadequate ventilation during multi-coat application
controls: Obtain SDS for anti-carbonation coating before work starts. Confirm resin type, VOC content, cure time, and respiratory protection requirement at point of use.

Establish continuous forced ventilation (mechanical fan or natural cross-wind) across scaffold platform during application and cure. Verify wind speed or fan output meets SDS requirement — minimum 0.5 m/s air velocity across work face.
Wear organic vapour respirator (cartridge type per SDS Section 8) fitted and checked before each coat application. Do not use P2 dust masks for solvent or resin vapours.

check scaffold platform before each shift for wet drips, overspray, or slippery surface. Clean or dry affected areas with absorbent cloth before resuming work. Prohibit barefoot or smooth-soled footwear on platform.
Apply first coat in thin, even passes. Do not re-wet or overload substrate. Allow full cure time per SDS before second coat — minimum 16 hours or as specified by manufacturer, verified in writing.
Establish wet coating exclusion zone on scaffold platform — barricade wet areas with warning tape and cones. Post 'Wet Paint' signage visible to all workers and building occupants.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or butyl per SDS) and hi-viz shirt or vest
Do not start second coat until substrate is fully cured and inspected for even coverage. Check for bare patches, thin areas, or colour mismatch — mark and fix before final coat.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply coating until: SDS is on site, ventilation method is installed and tested, and organic vapour respirator cartridges are confirmed current and fitted
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply second or final coat until: first coat is fully cured per SDS time, substrate coverage is uniform and inspected, and wind/weather conditions remain within cure window
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: forced ventilation fails, wind drops below 0.5 m/s, or organic vapour respirator cartridge is damaged, wet, or not fitted
🛑 STOP WORK if: rain or temperature drops below SDS minimum cure temperature during application or cure window
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold platform becomes slippery with wet coating and cannot be dried, or overspray contaminates adjacent work areas or building occupant spaces
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Confirm working at heights permit signed before each elevation or shift.
Record SDS receipt, ventilation test, cure times between coats, and coverage inspection sign-offs in site diary or QA register.
tell building management of work schedule, cure times, and ventilation method to manage occupied building disruption.
Obtain manufacturer's application data sheet or technical bulletin — confirm minimum temperature, humidity, and cure time before work starts.

ppe: Organic vapour respirator (cartridge type per SDS Section 8) — fitted before each coat application
Safety harness and lanyard (rescue-rated, secured to fixed anchor point per scaffold design)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify continuous forced ventilation across scaffold platform and organic vapour respirator fitted before each coat application.
monitoring.frequency: Before each coat application; continuous during work; after each shift before cure period
monitoring.evidence: SDS receipt logged; ventilation fan running or wind speed verified; respirator cartridge dated and fitted; scaffold platform cleaned and dried; cure time logged in site diary with supervisor sign-off; coverage inspection form completed

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold and fall arrest systems, enforce exclusion zone, check SDS
responsibility.WKR: Use harness and lanyard, wear respiratory protection, report faults

task_blocks_raw.task: Apply textured acrylic render finish coat
task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply textured acrylic render finish coat to all four elevations. Match existing colour and texture. Apply in suitable weather conditions. Cure per product specification. Final appearance to match existing or design intent.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of render spray or vapour — inadequate ventilation or respiratory protection during application
Fall from height — slippery scaffold platform from wet render splashes or overspray
Chemical exposure — skin or eye contact with uncured acrylic render causing irritation
Inadequate application — poor coverage, colour variation, or texture mismatch due to weather, contamination, or operator error
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of render spray or vapour — inadequate ventilation during application
controls: Read SDS on point of use before opening render product — note Section 8 respiratory and Section 11 toxicity limits.
Confirm weather window: dry, temp 15–25°C, humidity <85%, no rain forecast next 48 hours — stop work if conditions cannot be met.
Wet-suppress render spray using fine-mist water spray or air-aspirated application gun — prevent dry aerosol escape from nozzle.
Maintain natural cross-ventilation or position portable fan upwind to dilute vapour plume away from operator and building occupants.
Wear organic vapour respirator (per SDS Section 8) fitted over beard-free face — not P2 dust mask.
Establish exclusion zone (minimum 2 m radius) and tell building occupants of work schedule — prohibit entry during application.
check scaffold platform before each shift — remove wet render splashes immediately using damp cloth to prevent slipping hazard.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and face shield — change gloves hourly or if render contacts skin.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply render until: scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and weather conditions meet product specification.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow building occupants or adjacent workers into exclusion zone until: render is cured per SDS and overspray residue is cleaned from adjacent surfaces.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 15 km/h, rain forecast within 24 hours, or temperature falls below 15°C or exceeds 25°C during application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: organic vapour respirator becomes damaged, does not fit, or ventilation cannot be maintained.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold platform becomes wet or slippery and cannot be dried immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Verify working at heights permit is signed and valid before starting elevated work.
Confirm all operators hold current RIIOHS204E or equivalent working-at-height competency — sight evidence before start of day.
Brief all building occupants on exclusion zone, work schedule, and expected duration — provide contact number for concerns.
Keep SDS for textured acrylic render accessible on site for duration of task — make available to first aid responder if exposure occurs.
Record actual weather, start/end time, product batch number, and colour match confirmation on site log daily.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (per SDS Section 8) — cartridge changed per product manufacturer specification or when taste/smell detected.
Face shield (clear polycarbonate, impact-rated) — worn in addition to eye protection
steel-capped footwear— essential on wet scaffold platform.
hi-viz shirt or vest— minimise skin contact with wet render.

monitoring.frequency: before each work session (daily start and after any break >1 hour)

task_blocks_raw.task: check facade repairs and coating finish
task_blocks_raw.scope: Walk-over inspection of all elevations. Check coating coverage, colour uniformity, texture consistency, crack stitching visible, no defects. Identify any touch-up or remedial work required.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loss of balance or slip during walk-over inspection on wet or slippery platform
Struck by falling debris or tools — dropped inspection equipment or scaffold components during close-proximity assessment
Weather exposure — prolonged inspection in high wind, rain, or cold conditions causing loss of grip or concentration
Incomplete or defective repair — undetected coating defects, colour mismatches, or stitching inadequacy requiring rework
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — loss of balance or slip during platform walk-over inspection
controls: Confirm coating substrate is dry and grip tested before inspection platform walk-over commences.
Establish 1.5 m exclusion zone below inspection platform. Post signage and barricade zone with safety netting or catch net.
Conduct platform surface condition check before each shift — test foot grip, identify algae, moss, or wet patches, remove slippery debris.
Wear non-slip footwear with verified grip rating (AS/NZS 2210.3) — test grip on wet platform before starting.
Secure inspection torch, magnifying glass, and sample colour swatches in tool belt — never carry loose in hands.
Establish weather stop rule: suspend inspection if wind speed exceeds 40 km/h, rain reduces visibility below 10 m, or platform becomes visibly wet.
Brief all workers on defect identification criteria before inspection — photograph reference samples of acceptable colour match, texture consistency, crack stitch visibility.
check in pairs — one worker on platform, one spotter on adjacent scaffold bay. Spotter maintains visual contact and confirms platform stability.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start inspection until: scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder, handover certificate provided, and platform stability confirmed by independent check.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed with remedial work identification until: all defects photographed, documented, and approved by coating consultant or project manager.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: platform surface grip fails, becomes wet, or worker reports loss of balance or near-slip.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 40 km/h, visibility drops below 10 m, or rain renders platform surface unsafe.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold shows movement, sway, or structural concern — isolate and tell scaffolder immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tell building occupants of inspection schedule — coordinate noise, vibration, and access restrictions.

Record inspection findings on site log — defect location, type, remedial action required, sign-off by inspector and approver.
Brief spotter on communication protocol — hand signals or radio contact always during platform work.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

task_blocks_raw.task: Execute touch-up repairs and quality corrections
task_blocks_raw.scope: Address inspection findings. Patch and blend any coating defects, colour mismatches, or surface imperfections. Final curing and verification.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker overreach or loss of balance during high-elevation touch-up work on scaffold
Inhalation of coating or primer vapours — inadequate ventilation during localised reapplication of coatings
Chemical exposure — skin or respiratory contact with uncured touch-up materials
Colour mismatch or surface defects — inadequate blending or curing resulting in visible repair marks
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — overreach or loss of balance during touch-up work at elevation
controls: Verify scaffold is tagged 'Safe to Use' and handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses it.
Install edge protection (kick board and mid-rail) on all exposed scaffold edges where touch-up work occurs at height >2m.
check harness, lanyard, and anchor point for damage before each shift; do not use if damaged or anchor point capacity unknown.
Tie off to independent anchor point rated ≥10 kN before starting work; movement between anchor points only with continuous attachment.
Establish exclusion zone 3m radius below all elevated touch-up work; restrict pedestrian and vehicle access with signs and barriers.
Ventilate work area continuously during coating application; open windows and doors or use mechanical extraction fan to manage vapour.
Review SDS for coating product on point of use; identify skin contact, inhalation, and cure time controls before work starts.
Apply touch-up coating only within environmental window specified on SDS (temperature, humidity, wind speed); do not apply outside limits.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not access scaffold for touch-up work until: Scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and edge protection is installed and tagged.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply coating until: SDS on point of use, environmental window confirmed, and exclusion zone is established and signed off by Site Supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Harness, lanyard, or anchor point is damaged or anchor point capacity cannot be confirmed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Environmental window cannot be maintained (temperature, humidity, or wind outside SDS limits).
🛑 STOP WORK if: Worker overreaches beyond scaffold edge, or edge protection is damaged or incomplete.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm Working at Heights Permit is current and signed by Site Supervisor before each elevated task.
Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or current equivalent).
Provide SDS training on coating product to all workers before starting; confirm understanding in toolbox talk.
Brief occupants on active elevated work and exclusion zone; restrict occupied building access to area below touch-up work.
Record completion of touch-up repairs, colour match verification, and curing time in project quality log.
Conduct final inspection of blended coating and sign off on quality acceptance before demobilisation.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

steel-capped footwear— steel toe cap and slip-resistant sole complying with AS/NZS 2210.
Organic vapour respirator — cartridge type rated for solvent or epoxy vapour per SDS Section 8 (not P2 dust mask).

task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove all work platforms, tools, and debris from scaffold and site. Damp-dust building facade. Clean all occupied-building interfaces. Remove exclusion zones and barriers. Leave site ready for occupancy.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker slip or trip during platform cleaning, debris removal, or final inspection before demob
Struck by falling tools or debris — dropped equipment or unsecured materials during cleanup from scaffold platform
Inhalation of damp dust — liberation of settled dust during damp-wiping or dry-cleaning of facade
Collapse or instability — incomplete bracing or damaged components during scaffold partial dismantling
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — slip or trip during platform cleaning and final walkover
controls: Damp-wipe all settled dust from facade and scaffold using low-pressure water spray and cloth before any dry cleaning or tool movement.
Establish 5 m exclusion zone below scaffold during final cleanup and debris removal — no occupants or pedestrians permitted.
check scaffold for loose bracing, damaged ties, or missing components before cleanup commences — do not work on defective scaffold.
Secure all tools and small items in closed containers on platform — no loose objects permitted above head height of people below.
Wear harness attached to certified anchor point during all work on platform above 2 m — harness and anchor inspected before use.
Brief all workers on pedestrian traffic routes and occupant interface zones before cleanup starts — mark final walkover path with tape.
Remove debris only via waste chute or closed skip — do not throw materials from height.
Conduct final walkover of all occupied-building interfaces and common areas — confirm no dust, debris, or residual hazard remains.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove scaffold until: Site supervisor confirms all debris is cleared, facade damp-dust is complete, and final walkover sign-off is obtained.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit occupants to re-occupy affected areas until: all barriers are removed, area is clean, and post-work inspection is documented.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses grip or balance on platform — do not resume until cause is identified and corrected.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unsecured objects fall or escape exclusion zone — implement additional containment and investigate cause.
🛑 STOP WORK if: visible bracing movement, cracking, or damage occurs during cleanup — tell scaffolder immediately.
admin: Confirm scaffold remains certified and tagged until final removal — do not permit use of damaged or uncertified scaffold.
Obtain site supervisor approval before final walkover commences.
Record final area clearance and occupant notification in site diary.
Coordinate with building management to confirm access to common areas and interface zones.
tell occupants of final cleanup schedule and temporary access restrictions.

task_blocks_raw.scope: Dismantle scaffold, remove all site plant and equipment, final safety checklist, site induction close-out, handover to principal contractor and building management.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker loss of balance during final scaffold dismantling or inspection of platform before removal
Struck by falling scaffold components — dropped or misaligned members during dismantling sequence
Inadequate site restoration — incomplete removal of barriers, exclusion zones, or debris leaving occupied-building interface unsafe
Incomplete handover — missing documentation, safety checklist, or induction close-out creating liability gap
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Struck by falling scaffold components — member ejection or collapse during dismantling
controls: Establish exclusion zone below scaffold perimeter — minimum 2m radius — barricade with tape and signage before dismantling starts
Brief all workers on dismantling sequence and component drop zones — identify landing areas and confirm communication method before first member removal
Remove scaffold from top down — systematically dismantle horizontal beams first, then standards, then base; never force or lever members
Secure each removed member to designated stack area immediately — do not leave components unsecured on walkways or platforms
Use hand signals or two-way radio to communicate between dismantling crew and ground spotter — spotter remains in constant visual contact with all work
check all scaffold attachment points and base condition before final removal — photograph any cracks, deformation, or instability and report to Principal Contractor
Complete final safety checklist: all barriers removed, exclusion zones cleared, debris collected, access routes unobstructed, building services reinstated
Confirm site induction close-out with all workers — record names, dates and sign-off on project induction register
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not dismantle scaffold until: licenced scaffolder has verified erection method and base integrity, and exclusion zone is secured and signed off by Site Supervisor

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not hand over site to Principal Contractor until: final safety checklist is complete, all debris is removed, all workers have completed induction close-out, and Principal Contractor has conducted final walk-through
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold member shows cracks, bent sections, or loose connections during dismantling — do not remove until assessed by licenced scaffolder
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind exceeds 12 m/s or rain conditions affect grip and balance during elevated dismantling work — resume only when weather improves
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by occupants or unauthorised personnel — re-establish barrier and restart sequence only when zone is clear
